aliases.name: FN MAG
aliases.note: The Belgian-designed general-purpose machine gun the M240 is a US-built version of.

aliases.name: M240B
aliases.note: The current dismounted-infantry configuration; figures in this entry describe it.

massEmpty.sourceNote: M240B configuration, converted from the infobox's 27.6 lb, uncited on Wikipedia

length.sourceNote: converted from the infobox's 49.7 in, uncited on Wikipedia

barrelLength.sourceNote: converted from the infobox's 24.8 in, uncited on Wikipedia

width.sourceNote: converted from the infobox's 4.7 in, uncited on Wikipedia

height.sourceNote: converted from the infobox's 10.4 in, uncited on Wikipedia

cyclicRate.sourceNote: midpoint of the published, uncited base rate of 550-650 rounds a minute on the single-port gas setting; three higher adjustable gas settings are also published, up to 850-950 rounds a minute

effectiveRange.sourceNote: midpoint of the published, uncited 800-1800 m range, which depends on mount

capacity.sourceNote: M13 disintegrating-link belt, commonly carried in 100-round pouches; a 50-round assault pouch and the non-disintegrating DM1 belt are also published as feed options

images.alt: A black belt-fed machine gun on a plain background, seen from the left, with a rail-mounted optical sight, a folding bipod and a ribbed barrel jacket
images.caption: An M240L, a lightened variant of the M240 machine gun with a titanium receiver, fitted with an ELCAN optical sight. This entry's figures describe the M240B rather than the M240L pictured here.

images.alt: A soldier lying prone in a forest clearing firing a belt-fed machine gun on a bipod, with a burst of muzzle flash visible at the barrel
images.caption: A US Marine firing an M240B machine gun from a bipod during training in Australia, 2021.
